message.content:
**Answer:** One of the most iconic and widely recognized sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser) by Auguste Rodin (1889)**. Created in the late 1880s, it quickly became a symbol of romantic love and artistic innovation, and it remains one of Rodin’s most celebrated works. --- ### Why “The Kiss” stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin, a leading French sculptor who helped usher in modern sculpture. | | **Date** | 1889 – firmly within the 19th century. | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist blend; the figures are rendered with dramatic, almost tactile detail. | | **Impact** | • Became an emblem of the Romantic movement.
• Influenced countless artists and became a cultural icon.
• Its image has been reproduced in countless media, from postcards to modern advertising. | | **Legacy** | • The original marble version is housed at the Musée Rodin in Paris.
• Numerous casts exist worldwide, including a famous bronze cast in Washington, D.C. | --- ### Other notable 19th‑century sculptures While “The Kiss” is often cited as the most famous, several other works also achieved great renown: | Sculpture | Artist | Year | Significance | |-----------|--------|------|--------------| | **The Statue of Liberty** | Frédéric Baron Houdon (design), Alexandre Gros (sculpture) | 1886 | A monumental gift from France to the U.S., symbolizing freedom. | | **The Gates of Hell** | Auguste Rodin | 1880–1908 | A massive, complex work that influenced modern sculpture. | | **The Thinker** | Auguste Rodin | 1902–03 (early 20th) | Though technically early 20th, its conception began in the 19th and it remains iconic. | | **The Venus de Milo** | Unknown (ancient) | 150–100 BCE (but widely displayed in the 19th) | Ancient masterpiece that captivated 19th‑century audiences. | --- ### Bottom line If you’re looking for a single sculpture that epitomizes 19th‑century artistic achievement and remains instantly recognizable today, **“The Kiss” by Rodin** is the most fitting choice.
